chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ibn Faddal, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said:

A man from the Ansar came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I have been tested with a great matter. I had intercourse with my female slave, then I went out for some need of mine. When I returned from the road, I found my boy between the legs of the female slave. I kept away from her, and she became pregnant, then she gave birth to a female child after a period of nine months.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Retain the female slave; do not sell her, and spend on her until she dies or Allah makes a way out for her. If a mishap befalls you, then make a bequest that she be spent upon from your wealth until Allah makes a way out for her.'

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: The Ansar, the helpers of Medina
key_terms.لِعِدَّةِ تِسْعَةِ الْأَشْهُرِ: For a period of nine months

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a master who impregnates his female slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *lhuq al-awlād* (the attachment of offspring to the father) in cases of *ibāda* (concubinage), where the child is legitimate and inherits from the master. Imam al-Baqir’s directive to retain and maintain the slave-girl until death or birth underscores the legal obligation of *radāʿ* (nursing/maintenance) and ensures the child’s lineage is secured, a key topic in Chapter 7 regarding the establishment of nasab. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the father’s responsibility extends beyond mere acknowledgment to active financial support, reflecting the broader Islamic emphasis on protecting the rights of the mother and child in non-marital unions.
